reasons: No automated visual test appears in the packet.
The packet splits one grouped rule across two sections, so the exact selectors need a direct read of the file.

terms.meaning: the language that sets how page elements look
a page layout method that places items in rows and columns
a rule that applies only at certain screen widths
a set of steps describing how a style changes over time
a named value, written with two dashes, that rules can reuse

depends_on: the global stylesheet (not in the packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header comment
sections.what: The opening comment says the hero plant is built from schedule fragments and that the headline follows it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comment.

sections.name: .upload-copy
sections.title: Bleed spacing variable
sections.what: Sets how far the hero visual reaches past the normal page edge, scaled to screen width.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the plant picture reach the screen edges while text stays inset.
sections.watch_out: Other hero rules read this variable, so changing it moves the plant and its surrounding layout.

sections.name: .landing-nav
sections.title: Top navigation bar layout
sections.what: Lays out the top bar with items spread apart and centred vertically.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard layout for a header row.

sections.name: .landing-brand
sections.title: Brand name and shared label style
sections.what: Styles the brand name. The rule that follows starts a shared group that appears to cover the nav label, stage labels, figure caption and journey headings, giving them a small monospace uppercase look.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared label style keeps small headings consistent.
sections.watch_out: Because this group is shared, changing its monospace or uppercase settings changes several unrelated elements.

sections.name: .landing-journey strong
sections.title: Journey heading style
sections.what: Sets the spaced, uppercase monospace look for the journey headings. This is the end of the shared group above.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the three journey headings a technical label feel.
sections.watch_out: Edits here also affect the other elements in the shared group.

sections.name: .landing-nav-label
sections.title: Navigation label colour
sections.what: Dims the small navigation label and makes it slightly smaller.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the label quiet beside the brand name.

sections.name: .landing-hero
sections.title: Hero section grid
sections.what: Lays the hero out as two rows: the visual takes the flexible space and the copy sits below it. The block is at least most of the screen height.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the picture and headline both visible on a laptop screen.
sections.watch_out: The height depends on the browser window, so short windows may push the copy below the fold.

sections.name: .plant-hero
sections.title: Plant visual container
sections.what: Arranges the plant picture, its stage list and its caption in rows, and stretches the block past the normal page margins.
sections.why: Likely reason: uses the bleed spacing to reach the screen edges.
sections.watch_out: Negative margins can cause sideways scrolling on narrow screens if the bleed value grows too large.

sections.name: .code-plant
sections.title: Plant canvas sizing
sections.what: Makes the canvas fill the visual area's width and height, with a minimum height of 15rem.
sections.why: Likely reason: the canvas code reads its size from the page, so it needs a real size.
sections.watch_out: The canvas code reads the size on load and on resize, so a size change made only in CSS needs a resize event to be picked up.

sections.name: .ph-stages
sections.title: Stage list grid
sections.what: Shows the stage list as five equal columns with small gaps.
sections.why: Likely reason: one column for each of the five hero stages.
sections.watch_out: The column count is fixed here and changed again by the small-screen rule.

sections.name: .ph-stages li
sections.title: Stage item animation
sections.what: Gives each stage item a grid layout and a looping animation that changes its text colour, with a delay based on its position.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the stages light up one after another.
sections.watch_out: Delays come from list position, so reordering stages changes their timing.

sections.name: .ph-stages li span
sections.title: Stage progress bar
sections.what: Draws a thin progress line for each stage and animates its colour on the same loop, starting with its item.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each stage a visible fill as it becomes active.
sections.watch_out: The bar colour comes from a per-stage variable, so a missing colour leaves the bar invisible.

sections.name: .plant-hero figcaption
sections.title: Plant caption style
sections.what: Makes the figure caption small, dimmed and spaced slightly above the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caption is secondary text.

sections.name: .landing-hero-copy
sections.title: Copy column top padding
sections.what: Adds top padding to the headline column that grows with viewport height.
sections.why: Likely reason: moves the headline down a little on tall screens.

sections.name: .landing-hero-copy .eyebrow
sections.title: Eyebrow label spacing
sections.what: Adds space below the small label that sits above the headline.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates the label from the large heading.

sections.name: .landing-journey
sections.title: Journey three-column layout
sections.what: Lays the three journey steps out in three equal columns with a width limit and spacing above.
sections.why: Likely reason: presents the journey as three steps side by side.
sections.watch_out: The column count is fixed here and changed to one column by the small-screen rule.

sections.name: .landing-journey li
sections.title: Each journey step
sections.what: Gives each step a top border line, padding and a counter that numbers it.
sections.why: Likely reason: visually separates each step.
sections.watch_out: The counter depends on a counter name set on the parent list, so removing that setting breaks the numbers.

sections.name: .landing-journey strong::before
sections.title: Journey step numbers
sections.what: Adds an automatic step number before each step title.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the journey a numbered sequence look.
sections.watch_out: The number is written as a zero followed by the count, so step ten would show as 010.

sections.name: .landing-journey strong
sections.title: Journey step titles
sections.what: Makes step titles brighter, slightly smaller and lighter in weight.
sections.why: Likely reason: titles stand out from the body text.

sections.name: .landing-journey span
sections.title: Journey step body text
sections.what: Makes the text under each step muted, slightly smaller and loosely spaced.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps body text readable and secondary.

sections.name: .upload-copy .truth-note
sections.title: Truth note spacing
sections.what: Limits the width of the note under the upload area and adds space above it.
sections.why: The class name suggests a note about what the model is based on. The note text is not in this file.

sections.name: .evidence-ladder
sections.title: Evidence chip list
sections.what: Lays evidence levels out in a wrapping row with small gaps and no bullet points.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the evidence levels as a row of tags.

sections.name: .evidence-ladder li
sections.title: Evidence chip look
sections.what: Gives each evidence level a pill shape with a thin border and small uppercase monospace text.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes each level look like a tag.

sections.name: .evidence-ladder li + li::before
sections.title: Arrows between evidence chips
sections.what: Puts an arrow before every chip except the first.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the levels as a sequence.

sections.name: .evidence-ladder li:last-child
sections.title: Final evidence chip highlight
sections.what: Colours the last chip in the gold accent.
sections.why: Likely reason: marks the final level in the sequence.
sections.watch_out: The highlight follows list position, so reordering the list moves it.

sections.name: .upload-walkthrough summary
sections.title: Upload walkthrough summary
sections.what: Makes the expandable summary label bright, semi-bold and shaped like a clickable pointer.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows that the summary opens when clicked.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 760px)
sections.title: Small screen layout
sections.what: On screens 760 pixels wide or less, shows the journey steps in one column, the stage list in three columns, and hides the navigation label.
sections.why: Likely reason: fits content on phones.
sections.watch_out: With three columns, five stages wrap onto two rows.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion setting
sections.what: When the user asks for less motion, switches off the stage animations.
sections.why: Likely reason: an accessibility setting for people sensitive to movement.
sections.watch_out: The canvas code checks the same setting separately, so the two must stay consistent.

sections.name: .demo-tour
sections.title: Demo tour panel
sections.what: Places a dark floating panel in the bottom right corner and styles its heading, text and buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: a guided-tour popup that stays visible while the page is scrolled.
sections.watch_out: The panel is fixed on screen, so on small windows it can cover page content.

summary: Styles the landing page: the hero layout, the animated stage list under the plant picture, the three-column journey section, the evidence chips, the upload walkthrough summary, and a small demo tour panel.
purpose: Keeps the landing page's look separate from the rest of the app's styles.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the opening comment.
how: Sets the hero grid and plant layout, styles the stage list and its animation, styles the journey and evidence sections, then adds rules for small screens and reduced motion, and finally the demo tour panel.
inputs: Class names set by the landing components, plus shared colour and font variables defined elsewhere.
risks: Some selectors are grouped into one rule, so changing that rule changes several elements. Some colour and font variables are assumed to exist in a global stylesheet that is not in the packet.
debug: If the landing looks wrong on phones, check the 760 pixel rule. If the stage animation does not run, check the reduced-motion rule. If a colour is missing, check that its variable is defined globally.
